item.name: Pale Coral
entries: This blade has a bone white metallic basket hilt, and wails as it swings through the air. You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this sabre.

While wielding this weapon, you are resistant to necrotic and radiant damage, and can speak and understand Laneshi. You also gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet and can breathe underwater.

item.name: Pale Coral (Ensouled)
entries: This blade has a bone white metallic basket hilt, and wails as it swings through the air. You were able to acquire it before the laneshi did, and the spirit of a dead laneshi necromancer remains bound within.
You have a +2 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this sabre.

While wielding this weapon, you have a +2 bonus to AC, are resistant to Necrotic and Radiant damage, and can speak and understand Laneshi. You also gain a {@variantrule Swim Speed|XPHB} of 30 feet and can breathe underwater.

item.name: War Axe of the Blood Traitor
entries: {@i This heavy weapon resembles a battle axe but it's a bit larger and has a second, opposite axe blade. The additional blade slightly increases the variety of techniques available to the wielder and serves to overawe opponents.}
This weapon deals double damage on a normal hit and triple damage on a critical hit.

{@i {@b Deadly.} } Deadly weapons often have high-quality blades that hold keen, razor-sharp edges. With any successful attack, you can reroll up to one of the weapon's damage dice if it rolls a 1. You cannot reroll any die that has already been rerolled with another effect (such as the Great Weapon Fighting class feature or the savage attacker feat) and vice versa.

item.name: Cloak of Secret Shadows
entries: This jet-black cloak is reversible, with night-black fur on one side and shiny silver silk on the other. You have advantage on Dexterity ({@skill Sleight of Hand}) checks while you wear the cloak. Additionally, while wearing this cloak, you are unaffected when another creature uses its reaction to impose disadvantage on your attack rolls or determine their results.
The cloak's other powers depend on which side of the reversible cloak faces outward while you wear it. You can switch which side of the cloak is showing as an action.

entries.name: Black Fur
entries: You are silent and {@condition invisible} to magical sensors created by divination spells, and your presence doesn't trigger the {@spell alarm} spell or other magical alarms.

As an action, you can pull the hood up to become a flat, intangible shadow. While you are a shadow, you have resistance to cold and necrotic damage and to nonmagical bludgeoning, piercing, and slashing damage. You also can't move, take actions, or touch or interact with objects except those already on your person when you became a shadow. You can pull down the hood as an action, ending the effect.

entries.name: Silver Silk
entries: You are shielded from the effects of divination spells. You can't be detected by spells like locate creature, and divination spells that reveal information, such as detect thoughts or augury, make their predictions as if you don't exist.

As an action, you can pull the hood up to cast {@spell disguise self} from the cloak (DC 17 to discern that you're disguised). This disguise creates an exact copy of a creature you can see that is within 300 feet of you as you cast the spell.

item.name: Fey-Eye
entries: This smooth orb of lapis lazuli glows bears a glowing dwarven rune, an ever-watchful naiad spirit trapped within. As an action, you can speak a command word to activate the stone. For the next hour, the orb spins and twitches, as if watching for danger from all directions; you have advantage on initiative rolls and a +5 bonus to your passive {@skill Perception}. Once you use this property of the stone, you can't do so again until the next dawn.

item.name: Scale of Gegazol
entries: The largest scales shed from the undead dragon Gegazol can be used as a shield, though few Valikans are foolhardy enough to try and steal one from her lair.
You have Resistance to Cold damage while wielding this shield, even cold damage dealt by coldfire.

item.name: Scraglung Helmet
entries: This gruesome helmet is fashioned out of the flesh and innards of a seaborn troll. You can breathe underwater while wearing it.

entries.name: Acidic Biology
entries: You take 5 ({@damage 2d4}) acid damage when you don this helmet, and again at the start of each hour you spend wearing it.

item.name: Mithra's Pinion
entries: This golden feather is said to have lined the interior of the hero Mithra's cloak. While you carry this feather, you can use your reaction to wave the feather and give a creature you can see within 30 feet advantage or disadvantage on a saving throw, including death saving throws, before it attempts the roll. Once a creature has been the target of this item, it can't be affected by this item again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Location
entries: This magic item is kept on the person of Hrafen av Skeir, or in his chambers in his longhouse, Hrafensheim.

item.name: Wyrmbreath
entries: This beautiful smithing hammer shimmers with a faint prismatic light. You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. While you are attuned to this item, you gain expertise in checks you make with {@item smith's tools|PHB}.

This weapon has 2 charges and regains both charges at dawn each day. When you hit a creature with a melee attack, you can expend a charge to unleash a burst of elemental fury. The attack deals an additional {@damage 2d6} cold, fire, or lightning damage (your choice). Until the end of your next turn, you have resistance to the chosen damage type.

A single-edged, one-handed blade, not unlike a machete. The langseax is an extended version of the shorter seax—not quite a sword, but close enough to do the job. The langseax excels in close-combat ﬁghting.

entries.name: Special
entries: While you are wielding a langseax and either grappling a target or being grappled by a target, you have advantage when attacking that target with the langseax.

Named ‘bearded axe’ for the long blade that curves down from the bottom of the axe head. The design gives the axe a larger cutting area without adding more weight. Not to mention the hooked beard makes for a nasty backswing.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make an attack against a target that is wielding a shield, you can choose to make a special attack that does not deal damage. Instead, on a hit, you hook their shield and yank it from their hands to the ground unless they succeed on a DC 15 Strength saving throw.

It was only a matter of time before someone caught in a tight spot without their axe picked up their ice pick instead. The war pick is the same basic idea, but bigger, and rarer—war picks are most often wielded by clan chieftains or other honored warriors in a clan. You really do not want to be on the receiving end of this thing, especially if the blow strikes true.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make an attack with a war pick, your critical chance range is increased by one step. For example, if you would normally score a critical hit on a 20, you can score a critical hit with a war pick on a 19 or a 20. If you would normally score a critical hit on a 18-20, you can score a critical hit with a war pick on a 17-20.

Also known as a “hewing spear”, the atgeir is essentially a Valikan glaive—a long, bayonet-like blade ﬁxed to a spear-length haft that can be used for either stabbing or cutting. The weapon is lauded and admired for its ability to make short work of armor.

entries.name: Special
entries: The atgeir ignores AC from mundane armor (not including shields or magical armor).

item.name: Fur Armor
entries: Fur armor is usually made from thin leather lined with animal pelt, and while it does not provide much in the way of protection, it does help stave oﬀ the cold, giving a +1 bonus to your Warmth Rating. Fur armor made by the Svalr is often believed to be magical.

item.name: Gambeson
entries: A gambeson is a form of padded cloth armor, typically with a high collar to protect the neck. They can be surprisingly heavy and eﬀective at stopping a deadly blow, but they tend to be bulky, and harder to move in than thinner armor.

item.name: Lamellar
entries: Valikan warriors typically eschew heavy armor, as it is hard to make and to maintain. Those who can afford it wear chain mail, but there is a cheaper option for those who want more protection than that of layered cloth. Lamellar armor is made by sewing together many tiny plates called lamellae. Making lamellae only requires rudimentary blacksmithing skills (and the time to sew them together), making it more affordable to make and repair than mail.
The stats given here assume the plates are made of hardened leather, but lamellae can also be made of steel; metal lamellar uses the same statistics as splint.

item.name: Lamellar (Steel)
entries: Valikan warriors typically eschew heavy armor, as it is hard to make and to maintain. Those who can afford it wear chain mail, but there is a cheaper option for those who want more protection than that of layered cloth. Lamellar armor is made by sewing together many tiny plates called lamellae. Making lamellae only requires rudimentary blacksmithing skills (and the time to sew them together), making it more affordable to make and repair than mail.

item.name: Kite Shield
entries: A shield is made from wood or metal and is carried in one hand. Wielding a shield increases your Armor Class by 2. You can benefit from only one shield at a time.
The wielder has disadvantage on Dexterity (Stealth) checks.
If the wielder has a Strength score lower than 13, their speed is reduced by 10 feet.

entries.name: Special
entries: Using a kite shield makes walking more difficult. Anyone wielding a kite shield incurs a 5-foot penalty to their walking speed.

item.name: Heartseed Ring (Budding)
entries: This band of living ash wood contains knowledge of the Circle of Stoneraisers. This ring grants its wearer the ability to use maneuvers described in chapter 3 of {@i Raider’s Guide to Valika}.

This ring’s magic power is represented as maneuver points, which you can spend to use maneuvers. When a maneuver calls for a saving throw, use the save DC listed below or your maneuver save DC if your subclass grants you one, whichever is higher.

In this stage, a single green bud adorns the ring. The ring stores {@b 3 maneuver points}, and it regains {@dice 1d3} expended points daily at dawn. You can use the following maneuvers (save {@dc 13}):

entries.name: Tremorcraft (1 point)
entries: With a subtle movement, you shift the ground beneath your opponents. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 maneuver point to target one Large or smaller creature or object touching the ground within 30 feet of you, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be moved 5 feet horizontally in any direction.
You can move one additional target per extra maneuver point you spend.

entries.name: Uplift Ridge (2 points)
entries: As an action, when standing on stone or natural earth, you can spend 2 maneuver points to slam your foot against the ground to create a ridge of stone that emerges from the ground and lasts for 10 minutes. The ridge is 6 inches thick, 10 feet long, and 3 feet high.
The ridge grants cover to creatures behind it. A Medium creature has half-cover, while a Medium creature that is prone, or a Small or smaller creature, has total cover.

item.name: Heartseed Ring (Sprouting)
entries: This band of living ash wood contains knowledge of the Circle of Stoneraisers. This ring grants its wearer the ability to use maneuvers described in chapter 3 of {@i Raider’s Guide to Valika}.

This ring’s magic power is represented as maneuver points, which you can spend to use maneuvers. When a maneuver calls for a saving throw, use the save DC listed below or your maneuver save DC if your subclass grants you one, whichever is higher.
In this stage, the bud has grown and been encircled by small leaves. The ring has {@b 4 charges} and regains {@dice 1d4} points at dawn. You can use the following maneuvers (save {@dc 14}):

entries.name: Tremorcraft (1 point)
entries: With a subtle movement, you shift the ground beneath your opponents. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 maneuver point to target one Large or smaller creature or object touching the ground within 30 feet of you, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be moved 5 feet horizontally in any direction.
You can move one additional target per extra maneuver point you spend.

entries.name: Uplift Ridge (2 points)
entries: As an action, when standing on stone or natural earth, you can spend 2 maneuver points to slam your foot against the ground to create a ridge of stone that emerges from the ground and lasts for 10 minutes. The ridge is 6 inches thick, 10 feet long, and 3 feet high.
The ridge grants cover to creatures behind it. A Medium creature has half-cover, while a Medium creature that is prone, or a Small or smaller creature, has total cover.

entries.name: Alter the Board (3 points)
entries: Your control of the earth allows you to alter the positions of other creatures by shifting the very ground they stand on. As a bonus action, you can spend 3 maneuver points to target a number of Large or smaller creatures that are touching the ground equal to your proficiency bonus within 60 feet. Unwilling creatures must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw to avoid being pushed up to 15 feet along the ground in any direction.

item.name: Heartseed Ring (Blossoming)
entries: This band of living ash wood contains knowledge of the Circle of Stoneraisers. This ring grants its wearer the ability to use maneuvers described in chapter 3 of {@i Raider’s Guide to Valika}.

This ring’s magic power is represented as maneuver points, which you can spend to use maneuvers. When a maneuver calls for a saving throw, use the save DC listed below or your maneuver save DC if your subclass grants you one, whichever is higher.
In this stage, the bud opens into a fluffy white flower. The ring stores {@b 6 points} and recovers {@dice 1d6} points at dawn. You can use the following maneuvers (save {@dc 15}):

entries.name: Tremorcraft (1 point)
entries: With a subtle movement, you shift the ground beneath your opponents. As a bonus action, you can spend 1 maneuver point to target one Large or smaller creature or object touching the ground within 30 feet of you, which must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw or be moved 5 feet horizontally in any direction.
You can move one additional target per extra maneuver point you spend.

entries: As an action, when standing on stone or natural earth, you can spend 2 maneuver points to slam your foot against the ground to create a ridge of stone that emerges from the ground and lasts for 10 minutes. The ridge is 6 inches thick, 10 feet long, and 3 feet high.
The ridge grants cover to creatures behind it. A Medium creature has half-cover, while a Medium creature that is prone, or a Small or smaller creature, has total cover.

entries.name: Alter the Board (3 points)
entries: Your control of the earth allows you to alter the positions of other creatures by shifting the very ground they stand on. As a bonus action, you can spend 3 maneuver points to target a number of Large or smaller creatures that are touching the ground equal to your proficiency bonus within 60 feet. Unwilling creatures must succeed on a Dexterity saving throw to avoid being pushed up to 15 feet along the ground in any direction.

item.name: Ice Axe
entries: A short-nosed tool similar to a miner’s pick, useful for scaling walls of ice when climbing and typically used in pairs. Grants advantage on Strength (Athletics) checks made to scale ice.

If you have a free hand, you can use this item to make an offhand attack as a Bonus Action. The attack has a reach of 5 feet and one target. If you have {@feat Two-Weapon Fighting|XPHB} or {@feat Dual Wielder}, you add bonuses to attack and damage as normal. Otherwise, you do not add non-ability-score-based bonuses to the attack or damage roll, and the maximum ability modifier to the attack or damage roll is +0. This item does not count as a melee weapon even if you use it to make an attack. The attack deals {@dice 1d2} Piercing damage on a hit.

item.name: Leash
entries: A woven cord of leather, sometimes with a muzzle, ideal for keeping hunting dogs or other animals at your side. Grants advantage on Wisdom (Animal Handling) checks related to the attached animal.

item.name: Snow Goggles
entries: Designed by the Svalr, these goggles are frequently made from wood or bone, and feature thin slits or crosses that reduce the amount of light exposed to the eyes, helping prevent snow glare in bright areas. You automatically succeed on Constitution saving throws against snow-blindness.

item.name: Star Arrow
entries: An arrow tipped with a head that burns bright white when lit on ﬁre. Designed by Clan Sýr, these arrows not only burn with intense light, but catch the air as they fall, drifting slowly to the ground. Creates a light in the sky visible  or 1 mile.

This arrow can be fired at a creature at a cost of one Action and one Bonus Action, but it automatically misses if the creature is farther away than half of the weapon's normal range. If you hit a creature with this arrow, the creature gains the {@condition Burning|monstersofdrakkenheim} ({@dice 1d3} Fire) condition. The {@condition Burning|monstersofdrakkenheim} damage dice increases by one step (maximum {@dice 1d12}) for every 5 feet closer the target was to you than half of normal range.

item.name: Silk Tunic
entries: Tunics come in a wide range of cuts, but all are designed to conserve valuable fabric. Some are made of linen, others of wool—wool tends to be warmer, but linen is more comfortable against the skin if the wearer doesn’t have an undertunic. Silk can also be used to trim a tunic, but must be imported, making it rare, expensive, and a sign of incredible wealth.

item.name: Linen Tunic
entries: Tunics come in a wide range of cuts, but all are designed to conserve valuable fabric. Some are made of linen, others of wool—wool tends to be warmer, but linen is more comfortable against the skin if the wearer doesn’t have an undertunic.

item.name: Fullcloth
entries: Worn underneath other layers, fullcloth covers the body from the ankles to the shoulders and is made of layered linen and wool. Wearing fullcloth is a luxury generally reserved for when one is expecting hard travel, such as over a mountain pass, for example.

item.name: Linen Cloak
entries: Cloaks are a staple for travel, and some of the most elegantly embroidered and lavishly decorated garments available. They come in a broad range of materials, typically fastened with ornamental pins that serve as an indicator of status even more so than the cloak itself. Enchanted cloak pins that never come loose are highly sought after.

item.name: Woolen Cloak
entries: Cloaks are a staple for travel, and some of the most elegantly embroidered and lavishly decorated garments available. They come in a broad range of materials, typically fastened with ornamental pins that serve as an indicator of status even more so than the cloak itself. Enchanted cloak pins that never come loose are highly sought after.

item.name: Fur Cloak
entries: Cloaks are a staple for travel, and some of the most elegantly embroidered and lavishly decorated garments available. They come in a broad range of materials, typically fastened with ornamental pins that serve as an indicator of status even more so than the cloak itself. Enchanted cloak pins that never come loose are highly sought after.

item.name: Leather Cloak
entries: 20 GP, 4 lb

Cloaks are a staple for travel, and some of the most elegantly embroidered and lavishly decorated garments available. They come in a broad range of materials, typically fastened with ornamental pins that serve as an indicator of status even more so than the cloak itself. Enchanted cloak pins that never come loose are highly sought after.
You have a +1 bonus to armor class while wearing this cloak.

item.name: Valikan Ship Lantern
entries: A lantern designed for use in the rain and snow, with a brass enclosure that keeps it safe from wind and water. Casts {@variantrule Bright Light|XPHB} in a 30-foot radius and {@variantrule Dim Light|XPHB} for an additional 30 feet. Can’t be put out by water.

item.name: Sun Compass
entries: Grants advantage on Wisdom (Survival) checks made to navigate during the day.

item.name: Ice Fishing Kit
entries: A small bundle of tools used for cutting holes in thick ice and catching the fish and other aquatic creatures that swim beneath. Proﬁciency with this kit allows you to add your proﬁciency bonus when making a check to gather food in areas such as frozen rivers or lakes.

item.name: Ice Skates
entries: While on ice you gain an additional 15 feet of movement, and you make weapon attacks with disadvantage.

item.name: Skis
entries: Doubles your maximum speed when moving downhill on snow, halves your maximum speed moving in any other direction.

item.name: Ichor Sample
entries: This sample of the ichorous Vetra is all that remains of Tristram's dream of her. It is slowly self-replicating. Once per day, you can apply it to something metal to cause that item to corrode. If the item has an armor class or grants an armor class bonus, that number is reduced by 2. If the item is a weapon, it gains a -2 penalty to attack.

item.name: Tristram's Helm
entries: A gorgeous, antlered helmet whose enchantment has been forged by the pact between a mortal and a Spirit of Nature. This helm has a particularly unnatural bent to it, and it grants the wearer the following properties:

items: You can cast the {@spell eldritch blast} cantrip at will. Charisma is your spellcasting ability for this spell.
You can speak and understand Sylvan.

While attuned to this helmet, you hear the whispers of Vetra, a Spirit of Nature who lives in the Dark Oak Grove in the kingdom of Charneault. You gain a new flaw: "I act on my destructive impulses and temptations without guilt or concern for the future."

item.name: Ancient Ritual Knife
entries: You gain a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon. Its blade is cruelly serrated, and curved for maximum wound trauma. A hit with this weapon is always a critical hit.

item.name: Dream Town Soul Sword
entries: You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
This weapon was forged from the lucid soul of a Dreamer in Dream Town. You sometimes feel emotions radiating off of it.

If the sword is in this position as a result of your actions, it blames you for its predicament. While the sword is in your possession, you have terrible nightmares of Dreamers tormenting you. Whenever you complete a long rest, you must succeed on a DC 5 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you do not gain the benefits of a long rest. On a natural 1, you also gain a level of {@condition Exhaustion|XPHB}.

If the sword's predicament is not your fault, the soul does not blame you. The emotions you feel may vary, but the soul is always friendly when you speak of reaching the surface and/or defeating Kasimir Sundrinker.

item.name: Dieadem
entries: This diadem is made from finely polished bone with vertical slits running up the three main bone shards on its front. While attuned to the dieadem, you can focus on a pile of bones as an action to cast the {@spell Create Undead} spell. Once you have cast this spell, you can't cast it again until next dawn.
The dieadem can't animate bones if they are within a living creature or already animated into an undead form.

item.name: Aurelia's Tears
entries: A gold vial filled with holy water, Aurelia's Tears is an artifact from a long-forgotten civilization. Imbued with the powers of the goddess, it was carried by the high priest of the city to put to rest undead that were no longer needed, or as a defense against undead that broke free of their creator's control. The vial contains 20 uses of water. Once per day, you can refill 1 use of the vial by adding completely pure water to it. The vial will expel any water that is not pure.

entries.name: Destroy Undead
entries: You can use an action to anoint an undead with a single use of water from the vial. If the undead is CR 2 or lower, it immediately drops to 0 hit points and cannot use its Undead Fortitude trait. If the undead creature is above a CR 2, it must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failure, it takes {@damage 8d8} radiant damage, or half as much on a success.

entries.name: Sunlight
entries: As an action, you can activate this item, causing it to shed {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light}. If the vial has 10 or more uses remaining, it sheds {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 30- foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for an additional 15 feet. If the vial has less than 10 uses of water remaining, the radius is reduced to 15 feet of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} and 15 feet of {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light}. The light is sunlight and lasts for an hour. Once this property has been used, it cannot be used again until the next dawn.

entries.name: Turn Undead (Usable only by a good-aligned Cleric or Paladin)
entries: If you have the Turn Undead feature, you can use this item once per day to use the feature without expending your own use. Once used, this feature cannot be used again until the next dawn. If the sunlight property of this amulet is active when you use this feature, all undead have disadvantage on their saving throws against this feature.

entries.name: Raise Dead (Usable only by a good-aligned Cleric or Paladin)
entries: You can anoint a dead creature with 10 uses of water from the vial. The creature is returned to life as with the {@spell raise dead} spell. Alternatively, you may use 5 uses of water from the vial in place of the material components for the {@spell raise dead} spell

item.name: Enchanted Map of Nov Ostoya
entries: Created by a thieves' guild in Nov Ostoya, this map is printed on high-quality vellum and measures roughly 3 feet long by 2 feet tall. It is a map of the city of Nov Ostoya, showing all the major avenues and many of the smaller side streets and back alleyways in the Low Streets and the Heights.

When you speak this map's command word ("callidus"), a second map overlays the city in a glowing blue script, highlighting known routes through the sewers beneath Nov Ostoya. Secret doors and entrances into and out of the sewers and the city are marked in green, and dangerous areas donated in red, with golden motes identifying safe houses or friendly fences. This glowing overlay lasts for one minute, and then it fades away.

item.name: The Countess's Communion Set
entries: This kit consists of a polished brass bowl and keen {@item dagger|PHB} set within a wooden chest lined with black satin. Once per day, you can use this set to cast {@spell commune} as a ritual: You must spill humanoid blood with the {@item dagger|PHB} into the brass bowl, then drink the blood from the bowl. Commune cast in this way only contacts the Arch Daemon Sitri, regardless of what deity you were attempting to commune with.

After you complete the ritual, make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. You can choose to fail this saving throw. On a failure, for the next 24 hours, you are more likely to give into vices of violence and pleasure, and you gain disadvantage on Wisdom saving throws and advantage on Charisma checks.

The {@item dagger|PHB} from this set counts as a +1 weapon that requires attunement. Any time an attack made with the {@item dagger|PHB} hits, you hear a sigh of pleasure in your mind. If a creature is killed with this {@item dagger|PHB}, make a DC 18 Wisdom saving throw. On a failure, you are {@condition stunned} until the end of your next turn as waves of ecstasy course through you.

item.name: The Countess's Communion Daggers
entries: You have a +1 bonus to attack and damage rolls made with this magic weapon.
These daggers are only obtainable from The Countess's Communion Set. If you wield both daggers at once, you can make an additional attack as a Bonus Action, but without the +1 bonus.

item.name: Fingerbone of Shattered Vows
entries: Created by the hags in the Black Mire, the fingerbone is covered in burned runes and feels slimy to the touch.

As an action, you can snap the bone in half, releasing the spell. If within 30 feet of a cursed creature, the creature must make a DC 19 Constitution saving throw. If the creature is below half its maximum hit points, the saving throw automatically fails. On a failure, the creature becomes {@condition Stunned|XPHB}, and it begins reverting to its original form on its next turn. The full transformation takes 4 rounds, during which the creature can do nothing but howl in pain as its body bends and twists. At the end of its fourth turn, the target creature is fully returned to its original form, is reduced to 0 hit points and is stable, and is no longer cursed.

item.name: Seeds of Hope
entries: A vivid pink blossom unfurls to reveal three unremarkable looking green seeds, each just under 1 inch in diameter. Gifted to the characters by the dryad Annaë, these seeds represent the possibility of redemption and new life brought to the lands of Soma.

You can use an action to throw a seed to an unoccupied space of your choosing within 30 feet. When the seed hits the ground, it erupts in a 20-foot radius sphere of tangled vines and blazing light. The sphere functions as if under the effects of the {@spell entangle} spell. Additionally, any creature that starts its turn in the radius must make a DC 18 Constitution saving throw. On a failed save, it takes {@damage 4d6} radiant damage, and half as much on a success.

If you remove a seed from the blossom, plant it in the dirt or sand, and then water it, the seed produces an effect 1 minute later from the ground where it was planted. The GM can choose an effect from the following table, determine it randomly, or create an effect.

rows: 5d4 toadstools sprout. If a creature eats a toadstool, roll any die. On an odd roll, the eater must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or take 5d6 poison damage and become poisoned for 1 hour. On an even roll, the eater gains 5d6 temporary hit points for 1 hour.
A geyser erupts and spouts water, beer, berry juice, tea, vinegar, wine, or oil (GM's choice) 30 feet into the air for 1d12 rounds.
A treant sprouts. It is friendly to you and your companions and will do what it can to help you until it is destroyed, or until 24 hours pass and it loses interest.

An animate, immobile statue in your likeness rises. It makes verbal threats against you. If you leave it and others come near, it describes you as the most heinous of villains and directs the newcomers to nd and attack you. If you are on the same plane of existence as the statue, it knows where you are. The statue becomes inanimate after 24 hours.
A camp re with blue ames springs forth and burns for 24 hours (or until it is extinguished).
1d4 + 8 bright pink toads crawl forth. When a toad is touched, it transforms into a Large or smaller monster of the GM's choice. The monster remains for 1 minute, then disappears in a pu of smoke.

A fruit tree grows. It has 1d10 + 20 fruit, 1d8 of which act as randomly determined magic potions, while one acts as an ingested poison of the GM's choice. The tree vanishes after 1 hour. Picked fruit remains, retaining any magic for 30 days.

A nest of 1d4 + 3 eggs spring up. Any creature that eats an egg must make a DC 20 Constitution saving throw. On a successful save, a creature permanently increases its lowest ability score by 1, randomly choosing among equally low scores. On a failed save, the creature takes 10d6 force damage from an internal magical explosion.

A hole sinks into the ground, forming a well. The well is a cylinder with a radius of 10 feet and a depth of 30 feet and has stone sides. A narrow spiral stone staircase leads down along the wall. At the bottom of the well is a spring of fresh water 5 feet in diameter. A creature who drinks from the spring must make a Wisdom saving throw. On a success, they gain the ability to cast detect thoughts once a day. On a failed save, or if the creature drinks from the well after gaining detect thoughts, the creature takes 6d10 psychic damage as the screams of the damned ll their mind. The well disappears after an hour, harmlessly ejecting any creature or item within it to the nearest unoccupied space. Any water taken from the spring retains its properties for 24 hours.
A vivid pink ower sprouts. When it unfurls, it holds three more seeds of hope.

item.name: Dose of Bliss
entries: Bliss is a golden powder that has been pressed into a small bead about half an inch in diameter. If placed under the tongue, it dissolves over the course of 1 minute and  lls the user with a sense of profound euphoria. Pure relaxation overcomes the user and their worries are washed away in place of the effects of the drug.
If you are a humanoid and you consume this drug, you are  lled with a feeling of complete calm and happiness. You are under the following effects for the next {@dice 1d4} hours:

items: You automatically fail all attack rolls and saving throws.

If you use an effect that requires another creature to make a saving throw, the DC is 10 and they make their save at advantage. At the end of the {@dice 1d4} hour duration, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain 1 level of {@condition exhaustion}.

item.name: Lord's Lament
entries: The exact origin of this bottle of wine is unknown, but tales tell of a vintner from before the fall who fermented his grapes with a rare herb. This gave the wine a particularly smooth taste, but also had an unexpected side-effect: If a vampire drank from a humanoid who had consumed this wine, the humanoid's blood burned and blistered in the vampire's mouth and throat.

This bottle of wine contains five uses. As an action, you can consume a use of lord's lament. For the next 8 hours, you have resistance to necrotic damage, and any vampire who bites you takes {@damage 2d4} radiant damage. If you die, or if you are completely exsanguinated, this effect ends.

item.name: Sunstone
entries: The sunstone came to Trista's family several generations ago, when her ancestor was out foraging for plants and fell into a shallow ruin. The stone was set into the wall of the ruin, in the center of a sun-shaped mosaic. Injured and unsure how to escape, the ancestor pried the sunstone free and then laid down to sleep, hoping someone would come searching for her. When she awoke, her injuries were healed. She was rescued not long after, and she smuggled the stone into the city of Voyd. The healing properties of the stone have been forgotten over the generations, though Trista remains unusually hardy and resistant to disease.

A coin-sized yellow gem, the sunstone radiates {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} in a 5-foot radius. The light is sunlight. As an action, you can suppress the sunlight for 10 minutes, or you can increase the brightness so that it radiates {@quickref Vision and Light||2||bright light} in a 5-foot radius and {@quickref Vision and Light||2||dim light} for additional 15 feet for 10 minutes.
As an action, you can shatter the sunstone, destroying it and causing a burst of sunlight as in the {@spell sunburst} spell, originating from the sunstone.

entries.name: Attuned Healing
entries: While you carry the sunstone, you regain 1 hit point at the start of each of your turns (10 hit points each minute) as long as the sunlight is not suppressed. Once you have been attuned to this item for 24 hours, its overwhelming power deals 1 radiant damage instead of healing you. Once you have been unattuned to this item for 24 hours, this property reverts.

item.name: Bloodletter Axe
entries: This weapon has 5 charges. When you hit a creature with weapon attack, you can expend a charge to make a deep, {@condition bleeding|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} wound, dealing {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage to the creature. At the start of each of the creature's turns, it takes an additional {@damage 1d8} necrotic damage as the wound gushes blood.
The {@condition bleeding|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} effect lasts for 1 minute, until a creature uses an action to staunch the wound or it receives magical healing.
When you hit a creature with a critical hit using this weapon, it applies the {@condition bleeding|MonstersOfDrakkenheim} effect without expending a charge.
The weapon regains all expended charges each day at dawn.

items: You automatically fail all attack rolls and saving throws.
If you use an effect that requires another creature to make a saving throw, the DC is 10 and the creature makes the save with advantage.

entries: At the end of the {@dice 1d4} hour duration, you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or gain one level of {@condition exhaustion}.

item.name: Potion of Dead Blood
entries: This potion looks, smells, and tastes like humanoid blood, but it has been laced with a potent poison. An {@spell identify} spell reveals its true nature.

If you drink the potion, you take {@damage 2d6} poison damage, and you must succeed on a DC 15 Constitution saving throw or be {@condition poisoned}. At the start of each of your turns while you are {@condition poisoned} in this way, you take another {@damage 2d6} poison damage. At the end of each of your turns, you can repeat the saving throw. On a successful save, the poison damage you take on your subsequent turns decreases by {@dice 1d6}. The poison ends when the damage decreases to 0.
If you are a vampire and you drink this potion, the poison damage you take increases to {@dice 5d6}.

item.name: Undead Necklace
entries: While wearing this necklace, your creature type registers as undead and you have advantage on saving throws against being {@condition charmed} or {@condition frightened} by undead creatures.

item.name: Lesser Elemental Gem Weapon

entries: Once per day as a bonus action, you can speak the weapon’s command word and cause elemental energy to engulf your weapon. For the next 10 minutes, the weapon deals 1d4 additional damage. The additional damage is either acid, cold, fire, or lightning as determined by the type of gem installed on the weapon.

entries: {@note This item has been created from Salvage text in the book; it may not be exactly as the author envisioned, some information is assumed.}

Such a weapon offers a +1 bonus to attack rolls and damage rolls, and when the wielder hits with an attack using such a weapon, it deals {@damage 1d6} extra acid damage. Each of these rare items requires 10 days and additional materials worth 1,000 gp to make.

base.name: Assault Rifle
entries: Combining a high rate of fire with rifle-grade ballistics, the Assault Rifle is a staple weapon for all modern militaries. Dozens of variants exist on this general design, but all share the traits of a flexible and formidable weapon.

specificVariant.name: Lesser Elemental Gem Assault Rifle
entries: Combining a high rate of fire with rifle-grade ballistics, the Assault Rifle is a staple weapon for all modern militaries. Dozens of variants exist on this general design, but all share the traits of a flexible and formidable weapon.

base.name: Bellow Flute
entries: The traditional Obojiman instrument has gotten a second life as a swift club-like weapon commonly used by traveling performers. It is crafted from a special coral found all across the shallows, which naturally forms with dozens of tiny holes that run throughout the body of the instrumental weapon. When swung it emits a beautiful harmonic sound.

base.name: Blunderbuss
entries: This distinctive short-range firearm features a dramatically flared muzzle designed to launch shot in a wide spray. Most effective at close range, the Blunderbuss can be considered a precursor to the modern shotgun.

entries: This one-handed axe has a pick on the opposite end of the blade. You can choose to deal either slashing damage or piercing damage, depending on which end you use to attack. If you are proficient with axes, you can add your proficiency bonus on any checks made to climb a vertical surface when wielding it.

base.name: Twinblades
entries: Twinblades are martial melee weapons; double-bladed polearms that rely on the user's dexterity to keep them in constant motion.

specificVariant.name: Lesser Elemental Gem Twinblades
entries: Twinblades are martial melee weapons; double-bladed polearms that rely on the user's dexterity to keep them in constant motion.

entries.name: Special
entries: The massive bloodwood spears used by these giants are too large to be effectively wielded by Medium or smaller creatures.

However, individuals proficient in {@item carpenter's tools|PHB} who succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Nature}) check can reduce the size of the giant's spear to the equivalent of a {@item pike|PHB} ({@damage 1d10} piercing damage) and which inflicts the {@condition bleeding|GH} condition if targets fail a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw {@homebrew |(see Grim Hollow Campaign Guide)}.

entries: This hand crossbow has been modified to support two crossbow mechanisms, each one activated with a separate trigger. Unlike other weapons with loading, it can be fired twice before it needs to be reloaded. If you are proficient with a {@item hand crossbow|PHB}, you are proficient with a twinshot hand crossbow as well.

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a bola is knocked prone and has its speed reduced to 0 until it is freed. A bola has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to free itself. The DC for this check is equal to 8 + the proficiency modifier of the bola's thrower + the thrower's Strength or Dexterity modifier (thrower's choice). Another creature can attempt a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the same DC to free a target hit with a bola within 5 feet of it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bola's cords (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. If a creature is freed by a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or by dealing slashing damage to the bola, the bola is destroyed.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a bola, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

entries.name: Special
entries: Three main types of boomerangs exist in Eberron: the Adar boomerang, which does slashing damage, the Talenta boomerang, which does bludgeoning damage, and Xen'drik boomerang, which does piercing damage.

When you miss a ranged attack roll with a non-magical boomerang, it returns to you at the end of your turn. A nonmagical boomerang can be caught with a DC 10 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. Magical boomerangs return to you at the end of your turn, regardless of whether you hit or miss, and they can be caught automatically.
If you fail the {@skill Acrobatics} check or you do not have a hand free to catch the returning boomerang, it falls to the ground 10 feet away from you in a random direction.

entries: When thrown, the boomerang returns to an unoccupied space adjacent to you. As a reaction, you can choose to catch it.

base.name: Butterfly Staff
entries: Although it can be used as a weapon, the butterfly staff is more commonly used as a tool to catch small spirits and critters. Its tall haft is capped with a well-woven net, which is often made from sheep dragon wool.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make a grapple check while holding the butterfly staff, you can use the staff to target a Small or smaller creature that is up to 10 feet away from you. When you do so, you use your attack modifier for the weapon in place of your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. While grappling a creature in this way, you can't make another attack with the butterfly staff.

entries: These heavy honey dipper shaped clubs are traditionally used for mixing the giant vats of wax used by the Courier Brigade to seal packages and craft candles. They're now used by postal knights and adventurers as a useful defensive and offensive tool.

entries.name: Special
entries: While wielding a candlemaker's club, you can use a bonus action to extinguish a flame within 5 feet of you.

entries: This bladed circular disc is an unusual thrown weapon. It glides through the air, slicing through anything in its path. Warriors who specialize with the chakram can learn to throw it in such a way that it returns to them after cutting the enemy.

entries: This strange and intimidating weapon was made for fishing in the reefs and crags of the Shallows. Its long haft is tipped with a spherical array of thin sharp barbs, which gave the spear its title, as its silhouette is reminiscent of a blooming dandelion.

base.name: Field Spear
entries: Also known as the merchant's blade, the field spear was proven a useful and sturdy tool by the hundreds of merchants and travelers that use it in their expeditions across the island. Its shorter haft is roughly half the size of a standard spear and its tip is more similar to a wide blade or dagger than the traditional spear tip.

base.name: Goad
entries: Thay's slavekeeping history led to the development of a supposedly non-lethal weapon now used by many Thayan gateguards and houseguards to drive off would-be intruders when they want such undesirables to stagger away bleeding rather than end up as (inconvenient to explain or dispose of) corpses: the goad.

Goads are ten-foot-long (or shorter) whips tipped with a pointed-both-ends metal "finger" or a tiny grapnel with sharpened points. A goad does {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and has the finesse and reach properties, but unlike most whips, goads cannot coil around creatures or objects to entangle or {@action grapple} them, even if tipped with grapnels. The general attitude in Thay these days is that anyone who uses a goad on a slave is a wasteful fool, and that being attacked with one is an insult to the attacked. Most Thayans only see them used for crowd control.

entries.name: Special

It is a large hatchet-like axe mounted on the end of a long, curved handle, with a metal spike designed for thrusting mounted on the other end. The Znir gnolls do not sell myrnaxes, so they are exceptionally rare to see on the market.

Whenever you make an attack roll with a myrnaxe, you may choose which end to strike with, dealing either slashing or piercing damage with the attack if you hit. If you have multiple attacks in a turn, at least one attack must be made with each end.

entries: Immediately after hitting a target with the shears, if you have a free hand, you can use your reaction to pull the lever, snapping the blades together and dealing an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage to the target. If the triggering attack was a critical hit, you deal an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage. If this attack deals more than one-quarter of a creature's hit point maximum, you also {@table Losing Limbs|SGttEH|chop off one the creature's limbs (anything but the head) at the GM's discretion}. If this attack reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it is decapitated.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is actually a hollow sheath for a rapier or specially-made shortsword. The rapier or special shortsword is not included in the price of the sword cane; rapiers have their listed cost in the Player's Handbook and a specially fitted shortsword costs 20 gp instead of 10 gp but otherwise uses the normal statistics for a shortsword. The cane is made of strong hardwood and can be used as a weapon itself, using the listed statistics.

Its poor construction is the reason it's not often a weapon seen on land, though when used by a skilled fighter, it most certainly can be a formidable tool.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielding a zulaat, at the start of your turn, you must choose for the weapon to have either the Reach or the Double weapon property (see sidebar) until the start of your next turn. While a zulaat has the Reach property, it deals 2d4 slashing damage on a hit, and while it has the Double property, it deals 1d6 slashing damage on a hit.

A zulaat is a martial weapon developed by the Unity of Riedra. These weapons are normally forged of steel, but Chosen and Inspired warriors often carry zulaats created from sentira or crysteel. A zulaat is a double-ended weapon, comprised of a long central haft and a glaive's head at each end, and weights 10 pounds if made from steel or crysteel (or 9 pounds if made from sentira). It has the Two-handed and Special weapon properties.

Zulaats are supplied to soldiers in Riedra, not sold, and are exceptionally rare in Khorvairian markets—those found are typically contraband snuck outside of Riedra by a band of smugglers known as the Dream Merchants. Such zulaats, typically of the mundane steel variety, might be purchased (where available) for 150 gp.

entries.name: Special
entries: The massive bloodwood spears used by these giants are too large to be effectively wielded by Medium or smaller creatures.

However, individuals proficient in {@item carpenter's tools|PHB} who succeed on a {@dc 12} Dexterity ({@skill Nature}) check can reduce the size of the giant's spear to the equivalent of a {@item pike|PHB} ({@damage 1d10} piercing damage) and which inflicts the {@condition bleeding|GH} condition if targets fail a {@dc 12} Constitution saving throw {@homebrew |(see Grim Hollow Campaign Guide)}.

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a bola is knocked prone and has its speed reduced to 0 until it is freed. A bola has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to free itself. The DC for this check is equal to 8 + the proficiency modifier of the bola's thrower + the thrower's Strength or Dexterity modifier (thrower's choice). Another creature can attempt a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the same DC to free a target hit with a bola within 5 feet of it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bola's cords (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. If a creature is freed by a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or by dealing slashing damage to the bola, the bola is destroyed.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a bola, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

entries.name: Special
entries: Three main types of boomerangs exist in Eberron: the Adar boomerang, which does slashing damage, the Talenta boomerang, which does bludgeoning damage, and Xen'drik boomerang, which does piercing damage.

When you miss a ranged attack roll with a non-magical boomerang, it returns to you at the end of your turn. A nonmagical boomerang can be caught with a DC 10 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. Magical boomerangs return to you at the end of your turn, regardless of whether you hit or miss, and they can be caught automatically.
If you fail the {@skill Acrobatics} check or you do not have a hand free to catch the returning boomerang, it falls to the ground 10 feet away from you in a random direction.

base.name: Butterfly Staff
entries: Although it can be used as a weapon, the butterfly staff is more commonly used as a tool to catch small spirits and critters. Its tall haft is capped with a well-woven net, which is often made from sheep dragon wool.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make a grapple check while holding the butterfly staff, you can use the staff to target a Small or smaller creature that is up to 10 feet away from you. When you do so, you use your attack modifier for the weapon in place of your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. While grappling a creature in this way, you can't make another attack with the butterfly staff.

base.name: Goad
entries: Thay's slavekeeping history led to the development of a supposedly non-lethal weapon now used by many Thayan gateguards and houseguards to drive off would-be intruders when they want such undesirables to stagger away bleeding rather than end up as (inconvenient to explain or dispose of) corpses: the goad.

Goads are ten-foot-long (or shorter) whips tipped with a pointed-both-ends metal "finger" or a tiny grapnel with sharpened points. A goad does {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and has the finesse and reach properties, but unlike most whips, goads cannot coil around creatures or objects to entangle or {@action grapple} them, even if tipped with grapnels. The general attitude in Thay these days is that anyone who uses a goad on a slave is a wasteful fool, and that being attacked with one is an insult to the attacked. Most Thayans only see them used for crowd control.

entries.name: Special
entries: The myrnaxe is the signature weapon of the gnolls of the Znir Pact. It is a large hatchet-like axe mounted on the end of a long, curved handle, with a metal spike designed for thrusting mounted on the other end. The Znir gnolls do not sell myrnaxes, so they are exceptionally rare to see on the market.

Whenever you make an attack roll with a myrnaxe, you may choose which end to strike with, dealing either slashing or piercing damage with the attack if you hit. If you have multiple attacks in a turn, at least one attack must be made with each end.

entries: Although it's not much of a secret nowadays, the magical stone known as feather rock, which is used to craft these stone swords, was once coveted and kept hidden by the Nakudama. Even though feather rock is now commonly used by potion brewers, and the craft of making one of these swords is fairly common, the name has stayed the same.

entries.name: Guillotine
entries: Immediately after hitting a target with the shears, if you have a free hand, you can use your reaction to pull the lever, snapping the blades together and dealing an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage to the target. If the triggering attack was a critical hit, you deal an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage. If this attack deals more than one-quarter of a creature's hit point maximum, you also {@table Losing Limbs|SGttEH|chop off one the creature's limbs (anything but the head) at the GM's discretion}. If this attack reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it is decapitated.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is actually a hollow sheath for a rapier or specially-made shortsword. The rapier or special shortsword is not included in the price of the sword cane; rapiers have their listed cost in the Player's Handbook and a specially fitted shortsword costs 20 gp instead of 10 gp but otherwise uses the normal statistics for a shortsword. Each sword cane can only accommodate the weapon it was created for. While sheathed in a sword cane, the weapon is completely hidden and only a DC 20 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made while holding and inspecting the cane reveals its nature as a sheath. The cane is made of strong hardwood and can be used as a weapon itself, using the listed statistics.

entries: A tapper sack is a simple tool and weapon used by farmers. At the end of a fine, yet sturdy, braided cord is a simple bag which has been filled with sand. Although it's not very flashy, in the hands of a skilled adventurer this humble weapon packs quite a punch.

base.name: Vaulter's Axe
entries: The vaulter's axe was designed by the Rangers of the Greenward Path for exploring the Brackwater Wetlands. Its tall haft allows wielders of the axe to easily check water depths and vault over obstacles. To this day it's a useful tool for anyone exploring the eastern side of the island.

base.name: Vertebrae Sword
entries: The jagged vertebrae sword of a fishfolk warrior can barely be called a sword. Locals would say it's better described as a makeshift weapon crafted from a fish skeleton and sea trash. Its poor construction is the reason it's not often a weapon seen on land, though when used by a skilled fighter, it most certainly can be a formidable tool.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you successfully hit a creature with a vertebrae sword, you can use a bonus action to rake and twist the weapon, breaking off some of the sword's boney barbs and dealing an extra 1d8 piercing damage. The vertebrae sword can only be used in this way 5 times before it becomes unusable as a weapon.

entries: A yklwa (pronounced YICK-ul-wah) is a simple melee weapon that is the traditional weapon of Chultan warriors. A yklwa consists of a 3-foot wooden shaft with a steel or stone blade up to 18 inches long. Although it has the thrown weapon property, the yklwa is not well balanced for throwing.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielding a zulaat, at the start of your turn, you must choose for the weapon to have either the Reach or the Double weapon property (see sidebar) until the start of your next turn. While a zulaat has the Reach property, it deals 2d4 slashing damage on a hit, and while it has the Double property, it deals 1d6 slashing damage on a hit.

A zulaat is a martial weapon developed by the Unity of Riedra. These weapons are normally forged of steel, but Chosen and Inspired warriors often carry zulaats created from sentira or crysteel. A zulaat is a double-ended weapon, comprised of a long central haft and a glaive's head at each end, and weights 10 pounds if made from steel or crysteel (or 9 pounds if made from sentira). It has the Two-handed and Special weapon properties.

Zulaats are supplied to soldiers in Riedra, not sold, and are exceptionally rare in Khorvairian markets—those found are typically contraband snuck outside of Riedra by a band of smugglers known as the Dream Merchants. Such zulaats, typically of the mundane steel variety, might be purchased (where available) for 150 gp.

base.name: Bellow Flute
entries: The traditional Obojiman instrument has gotten a second life as a swift club-like weapon commonly used by traveling performers. It is crafted from a special coral found all across the shallows, which naturally forms with dozens of tiny holes that run throughout the body of the instrumental weapon. When swung it emits a beautiful harmonic sound.

entries: The massive bloodwood spears used by these giants are too large to be effectively wielded by Medium or smaller creatures.

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a bola is knocked prone and has its speed reduced to 0 until it is freed. A bola has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to free itself. The DC for this check is equal to 8 + the proficiency modifier of the bola's thrower + the thrower's Strength or Dexterity modifier (thrower's choice). Another creature can attempt a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the same DC to free a target hit with a bola within 5 feet of it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bola's cords (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. If a creature is freed by a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or by dealing slashing damage to the bola, the bola is destroyed.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a bola, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

entries.name: Special
entries: Three main types of boomerangs exist in Eberron: the Adar boomerang, which does slashing damage, the Talenta boomerang, which does bludgeoning damage, and Xen'drik boomerang, which does piercing damage.

When you miss a ranged attack roll with a non-magical boomerang, it returns to you at the end of your turn. A nonmagical boomerang can be caught with a DC 10 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. Magical boomerangs return to you at the end of your turn, regardless of whether you hit or miss, and they can be caught automatically.
If you fail the {@skill Acrobatics} check or you do not have a hand free to catch the returning boomerang, it falls to the ground 10 feet away from you in a random direction.

base.name: Butterfly Staff
entries: Although it can be used as a weapon, the butterfly staff is more commonly used as a tool to catch small spirits and critters. Its tall haft is capped with a well-woven net, which is often made from sheep dragon wool.

While grappling a creature in this way, you can't make another attack with the butterfly staff.

base.name: Goad
entries: Thay's slavekeeping history led to the development of a supposedly non-lethal weapon now used by many Thayan gateguards and houseguards to drive off would-be intruders when they want such undesirables to stagger away bleeding rather than end up as (inconvenient to explain or dispose of) corpses: the goad.

Goads are ten-foot-long (or shorter) whips tipped with a pointed-both-ends metal "finger" or a tiny grapnel with sharpened points. A goad does {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and has the finesse and reach properties, but unlike most whips, goads cannot coil around creatures or objects to entangle or {@action grapple} them, even if tipped with grapnels. The general attitude in Thay these days is that anyone who uses a goad on a slave is a wasteful fool, and that being attacked with one is an insult to the attacked. Most Thayans only see them used for crowd control.

entries: This weapon is actually a hollow sheath for a rapier or specially-made shortsword. entries.name: Special
entries: When wielding a zulaat, at the start of your turn, you must choose for the weapon to have either the Reach or the Double weapon property (see sidebar) until the start of your next turn. While a zulaat has the Reach property, it deals 2d4 slashing damage on a hit, and while it has the Double property, it deals 1d6 slashing damage on a hit.

A zulaat is a martial weapon developed by the Unity of Riedra. These weapons are normally forged of steel, but Chosen and Inspired warriors often carry zulaats created from sentira or crysteel. A zulaat is a double-ended weapon, comprised of a long central haft and a glaive's head at each end, and weights 10 pounds if made from steel or crysteel (or 9 pounds if made from sentira). It has the Two-handed and Special weapon properties.

Zulaats are supplied to soldiers in Riedra, not sold, and are exceptionally rare in Khorvairian markets—those found are typically contraband snuck outside of Riedra by a band of smugglers known as the Dream Merchants. Such zulaats, typically of the mundane steel variety, might be purchased (where available) for 150 gp.

entries: The massive bloodwood spears used by these giants are too large to be effectively wielded by Medium or smaller creatures.

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a bola is knocked prone and has its speed reduced to 0 until it is freed. A bola has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to free itself. The DC for this check is equal to 8 + the proficiency modifier of the bola's thrower + the thrower's Strength or Dexterity modifier (thrower's choice). Another creature can attempt a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the same DC to free a target hit with a bola within 5 feet of it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bola's cords (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. If a creature is freed by a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or by dealing slashing damage to the bola, the bola is destroyed.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a bola, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

entries.name: Special
entries: Three main types of boomerangs exist in Eberron: the Adar boomerang, which does slashing damage, the Talenta boomerang, which does bludgeoning damage, and Xen'drik boomerang, which does piercing damage.

When you miss a ranged attack roll with a non-magical boomerang, it returns to you at the end of your turn. A nonmagical boomerang can be caught with a DC 10 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. Magical boomerangs return to you at the end of your turn, regardless of whether you hit or miss, and they can be caught automatically.
If you fail the {@skill Acrobatics} check or you do not have a hand free to catch the returning boomerang, it falls to the ground 10 feet away from you in a random direction.

base.name: Butterfly Staff
entries: Although it can be used as a weapon, the butterfly staff is more commonly used as a tool to catch small spirits and critters. Its tall haft is capped with a well-woven net, which is often made from sheep dragon wool.

entries.name: Special

While grappling a creature in this way, you can't make another attack with the butterfly staff.

base.name: Goad
entries: Thay's slavekeeping history led to the development of a supposedly non-lethal weapon now used by many Thayan gateguards and houseguards to drive off would-be intruders when they want such undesirables to stagger away bleeding rather than end up as (inconvenient to explain or dispose of) corpses: the goad.

Goads are ten-foot-long (or shorter) whips tipped with a pointed-both-ends metal "finger" or a tiny grapnel with sharpened points. A goad does {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and has the finesse and reach properties, but unlike most whips, goads cannot coil around creatures or objects to entangle or {@action grapple} them, even if tipped with grapnels. The general attitude in Thay these days is that anyone who uses a goad on a slave is a wasteful fool, and that being attacked with one is an insult to the attacked. Most Thayans only see them used for crowd control.

Whenever you make an attack roll with a myrnaxe, you may choose which end to strike with, dealing either slashing or piercing damage with the attack if you hit. If you have multiple attacks in a turn, at least one attack must be made with each end.

base.name: Nakudama Bubble Rod
entries: The Nakudama bubble rod is most recognizable by the curious sounds it produces when used. The wet descending whistle of multiple water filled glass marbles shot from the end of the oblong tube, quickly followed by the unmistakable pop of the ammunition as they hit their target.

entries.name: Special
entries: The orc double axe was created by the Ghaash'kala orcs of the Demon Wastes. An orc double axe may be wielded as either a double weapon that deals {@damage 1d6} slashing damage, or a heavy weapon that deals {@damage d10} slashing damage. A wielder may switch from one way to the other as an object interaction on their turn, before any attack rolls are made.

base.name: Secret Stone Sword

entries.name: Guillotine
entries: Immediately after hitting a target with the shears, if you have a free hand, you can use your reaction to pull the lever, snapping the blades together and dealing an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage to the target. If the triggering attack was a critical hit, you deal an extra {@damage 1d12} slashing damage. If this attack deals more than one-quarter of a creature's hit point maximum, you also {@table Losing Limbs|SGttEH|chop off one the creature's limbs (anything but the head) at the GM's discretion}. If this attack reduces a creature to 0 hit points, it is decapitated.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is actually a hollow sheath for a rapier or specially-made shortsword. The rapier or special shortsword is not included in the price of the sword cane; rapiers have their listed cost in the Player's Handbook and a specially fitted shortsword costs 20 gp instead of 10 gp but otherwise uses the normal statistics for a shortsword. Each sword cane can only accommodate the weapon it was created for. While sheathed in a sword cane, the weapon is completely hidden and only a DC 20 Intelligence ({@skill Investigation}) check made while holding and inspecting the cane reveals its nature as a sheath. The cane is made of strong hardwood and can be used as a weapon itself, using the listed statistics.

base.name: Vaulter's Axe
entries: The vaulter's axe was designed by the Rangers of the Greenward Path for exploring the Brackwater Wetlands. Its tall haft allows wielders of the axe to easily check water depths and vault over obstacles. To this day it's a useful tool for anyone exploring the eastern side of the island.

base.name: Vertebrae Sword
entries: The jagged vertebrae sword of a fishfolk warrior can barely be called a sword. Locals would say it's better described as a makeshift weapon crafted from a fish skeleton and sea trash. Its poor construction is the reason it's not often a weapon seen on land, though when used by a skilled fighter, it most certainly can be a formidable tool.

The vertebrae sword can only be used in this way 5 times before it becomes unusable as a weapon.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielding a zulaat, at the start of your turn, you must choose for the weapon to have either the Reach or the Double weapon property (see sidebar) until the start of your next turn. While a zulaat has the Reach property, it deals 2d4 slashing damage on a hit, and while it has the Double property, it deals 1d6 slashing damage on a hit.

A zulaat is a martial weapon developed by the Unity of Riedra. These weapons are normally forged of steel, but Chosen and Inspired warriors often carry zulaats created from sentira or crysteel. A zulaat is a double-ended weapon, comprised of a long central haft and a glaive's head at each end, and weights 10 pounds if made from steel or crysteel (or 9 pounds if made from sentira). It has the Two-handed and Special weapon properties.

Zulaats are supplied to soldiers in Riedra, not sold, and are exceptionally rare in Khorvairian markets—those found are typically contraband snuck outside of Riedra by a band of smugglers known as the Dream Merchants. Such zulaats, typically of the mundane steel variety, might be purchased (where available) for 150 gp.

entries.name: Special
entries: A Large or smaller creature hit by a bola is knocked prone and has its speed reduced to 0 until it is freed. A bola has no effect on creatures that are formless, or creatures that are Huge or larger. A creature can use its action to make a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) or Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check to free itself. The DC for this check is equal to 8 + the proficiency modifier of the bola's thrower + the thrower's Strength or Dexterity modifier (thrower's choice). Another creature can attempt a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the same DC to free a target hit with a bola within 5 feet of it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bola's cords (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. If a creature is freed by a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or by dealing slashing damage to the bola, the bola is destroyed.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a bola, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

The DC for this check is equal to 8 + the proficiency modifier of the bola's thrower + the thrower's Strength or Dexterity modifier (thrower's choice). Another creature can attempt a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check against the same DC to free a target hit with a bola within 5 feet of it. Dealing 5 slashing damage to the bola's cords (AC 10) also frees the creature without harming it. If a creature is freed by a Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check or by dealing slashing damage to the bola, the bola is destroyed.
When you use an action, bonus action, or reaction to attack with a bola, you can make only one attack regardless of the number of attacks you can normally make.

entries.name: Special
entries: Three main types of boomerangs exist in Eberron: the Adar boomerang, which does slashing damage, the Talenta boomerang, which does bludgeoning damage, and Xen'drik boomerang, which does piercing damage.

When you miss a ranged attack roll with a non-magical boomerang, it returns to you at the end of your turn. A nonmagical boomerang can be caught with a DC 10 Dexterity ({@skill Acrobatics}) check. Magical boomerangs return to you at the end of your turn, regardless of whether you hit or miss, and they can be caught automatically.
If you fail the {@skill Acrobatics} check or you do not have a hand free to catch the returning boomerang, it falls to the ground 10 feet away from you in a random direction.

base.name: Butterfly Staff
entries: Although it can be used as a weapon, the butterfly staff is more commonly used as a tool to catch small spirits and critters. Its tall haft is capped with a well-woven net, which is often made from sheep dragon wool.

entries.name: Special

When you do so, you use your attack modifier for the weapon in place of your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. While grappling a creature in this way, you can't make another attack with the butterfly staff.

base.name: Goad
entries: Thay's slavekeeping history led to the development of a supposedly non-lethal weapon now used by many Thayan gateguards and houseguards to drive off would-be intruders when they want such undesirables to stagger away bleeding rather than end up as (inconvenient to explain or dispose of) corpses: the goad.

Goads are ten-foot-long (or shorter) whips tipped with a pointed-both-ends metal "finger" or a tiny grapnel with sharpened points. A goad does {@damage 1d6} slashing damage and has the finesse and reach properties, but unlike most whips, goads cannot coil around creatures or objects to entangle or {@action grapple} them, even if tipped with grapnels. The general attitude in Thay these days is that anyone who uses a goad on a slave is a wasteful fool, and that being attacked with one is an insult to the attacked. Most Thayans only see them used for crowd control.

The Znir gnolls do not sell myrnaxes, so they are exceptionally uncommon to see on the market.

Whenever you make an attack roll with a myrnaxe, you may choose which end to strike with, dealing either slashing or piercing damage with the attack if you hit. If you have multiple attacks in a turn, at least one attack must be made with each end.

entries.name: Special
entries: This weapon is actually a hollow sheath for a rapier or specially-made shortsword. The rapier or special shortsword is not included in the price of the sword cane; rapiers have their listed cost in the Player's Handbook and a specially fitted shortsword costs 20 gp instead of 10 gp but otherwise uses the normal statistics for a shortsword. The cane is made of strong hardwood and can be used as a weapon itself, using the listed statistics.

entries.name: Special
entries: When wielding a zulaat, at the start of your turn, you must choose for the weapon to have either the Reach or the Double weapon property (see sidebar) until the start of your next turn. While a zulaat has the Reach property, it deals 2d4 slashing damage on a hit, and while it has the Double property, it deals 1d6 slashing damage on a hit.

A zulaat is a martial weapon developed by the Unity of Riedra. These weapons are normally forged of steel, but Chosen and Inspired warriors often carry zulaats created from sentira or crysteel. A zulaat is a double-ended weapon, comprised of a long central haft and a glaive's head at each end, and weights 10 pounds if made from steel or crysteel (or 9 pounds if made from sentira). It has the Two-handed and Special weapon properties.

Zulaats are supplied to soldiers in Riedra, not sold, and are exceptionally uncommon in Khorvairian markets—those found are typically contraband snuck outside of Riedra by a band of smugglers known as the Dream Merchants. Such zulaats, typically of the mundane steel variety, might be purchased (where available) for 150 gp.

A zulaat is a martial weapon developed by the Unity of Riedra. These weapons are normally forged of steel, but Chosen and Inspired warriors often carry zulaats created from sentira or crysteel. A zulaat is a double-ended weapon, comprised of a long central haft and a glaive's head at each end, and weights 10 pounds if made from steel or crysteel (or 9 pounds if made from sentira). It has the Two-handed and Special weapon properties.

Zulaats are supplied to soldiers in Riedra, not sold, and are exceptionally uncommon in Khorvairian markets—those found are typically contraband snuck outside of Riedra by a band of smugglers known as the Dream Merchants. Such zulaats, typically of the mundane steel variety, might be purchased (where available) for 150 gp.

item.name: Weapon of the Heart's Desire

entries: Fiends often bestow these elegant weapons on those who  serve them. While they vary in appearance, they possess  décor, materials, and designs relating to the daemon that  created it. For example, a mace given to a follower of Tor mach may be forged of dark iron that is constantly stained  with blood, while a rapier created by Beleth may have a bell  that hangs from its pommel or sharp barbs along the guard. While you are Attuned to this weapon, you have Advan tage on Wisdom (Insight) and Charisma (Deception) checks.

base.name: Butterfly Staff
entries: Although it can be used as a weapon, the butterfly staff is more commonly used as a tool to catch small spirits and critters. Its tall haft is capped with a well-woven net, which is often made from sheep dragon wool.

entries.name: Special
entries: When you make a grapple check while holding the butterfly staff, you can use the staff to target a Small or smaller creature that is up to 10 feet away from you. When you do so, you use your attack modifier for the weapon in place of your Strength ({@skill Athletics}) check. While grappling a creature in this way, you can't make another attack with the butterfly staff.

entries.name: Special
entries: The myrnaxe is the signature weapon of the gnolls of the Znir Pact. It is a large hatchet-like axe mounted on the end of a long, curved handle, with a metal spike designed for thrusting mounted on the other end. The Znir gnolls do not sell myrnaxes, so they are exceptionally rare to see on the market.

Whenever you make an attack roll with a myrnaxe, you may choose which end to strike with, dealing either slashing or piercing damage with the attack if you hit. If you have multiple attacks in a turn, at least one attack must be made with each end.

An orc double axe may be wielded as either a double weapon that deals {@damage 1d6} slashing damage, or a heavy weapon that deals {@damage d10} slashing damage. A wielder may switch from one way to the other as an object interaction on their turn, before any attack rolls are made.
